skill.name: npm-git-install
skill.description: Install npm packages directly from GitHub repositories with Git URL syntax for private repos, branches, tags, and unreleased packages.
skill.summary: Guide npm Git URL installs for public, private, forked, and unreleased Node.js packages.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown syntax, placeholder paths, or documentation links rather than executable code. Confirmed risks remain around privileged commands, token handling, npmrc configuration, authenticated Git installs, mutable remote packages, and persistent shell or credential configuration. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed skill text.

remediation.issue: Token-bearing Git URLs and npmrc examples can expose GitHub credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Remove token-in-URL examples, prefer SSH or scoped npm auth, and warn users not to log tokenized install commands.

remediation.issue: Mutable branch installs and npm prepare scripts create supply-chain execution risk.
remediation.suggestion: Use tags or commit hashes in production examples and require review of lifecycle scripts before installation.

remediation.issue: The troubleshooting section includes sudo and persistent shell configuration changes.
remediation.suggestion: Replace broad sudo chown guidance with user-level npm configuration and require confirmation before editing shell startup files.

remediation.issue: The Git credential helper store recommendation can persist credentials insecurely.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer platform keychain helpers or short-lived tokens, and document the storage risk of credential.helper store.

content.user_title: Install npm Packages from Git Repositories
content.value_statement: Teams often need packages from private repositories, forks, or unreleased branches. This skill shows npm Git URL syntax, authentication options, verification steps, and maintenance commands.
actual_capabilities: Shows HTTPS, SSH, and GitHub shorthand formats for npm installs.
Explains branch, tag, commit, and default branch selectors.
Covers private repository access with SSH keys, tokens, environment variables, and npmrc.
Provides commands to verify global package locations and installed binaries.
Lists update, uninstall, cache, and common troubleshooting commands.
limitations: It does not verify repository trustworthiness or package contents.
It does not remove npm lifecycle script risks from Git installs.
It requires working Git, Node.js, network access, and user-managed credentials.
Some examples use mutable branches and should be pinned for production.

use_cases.description: Install a package from a branch, tag, or commit before it is published to the npm registry.

use_cases.title: Document Git Dependency Options
use_cases.description: Compare npm Git URL formats and write team guidance for forks, branches, and private repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Install a Public Git Package
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a public repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to install an npm package from a public GitHub repository. Include tag and commit options.

prompt_templates.title: Use a Private Repository
prompt_templates.scenario: Authenticated install for a private package.
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through installing an npm package from a private GitHub repository. Compare SSH and token-based authentication.

prompt_templates.title: Pin and Verify a Dependency
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me pin a Git-based npm dependency to a stable tag or commit. Include verification and lockfile steps.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Git Install Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose my npm Git install failure. Check Git access, package scripts, cache issues, global paths, and authentication.

output_examples.input: Install a package from a GitHub tag.
output: Use the repository URL with a tag selector.
Prefer a release tag or commit for reproducible installs.
Verify the installed package and commit the lockfile.

output_examples.input: Install a private package for a team project.
output: Choose SSH when developers already have GitHub keys configured.
Use least-privilege tokens only when SSH is not available.
Avoid storing tokens in package files or shared logs.

output_examples.input: Fix a global install permission error.
output: Prefer a user-level npm prefix over broad system ownership changes.
Confirm shell path changes before editing startup files.
Reopen the terminal and verify the binary location.

best_practices: Pin production dependencies to release tags or commit hashes.
Use SSH keys or environment-managed tokens with least privilege.
Review npm lifecycle scripts before installing code from Git repositories.
anti_patterns: Installing mutable main branches in production.
Embedding personal access tokens in dependency files or logs.
Using sudo or changing global directories without explicit approval.

faq.question: Can npm install directly from GitHub?
faq.answer: Yes. npm accepts Git URLs, GitHub shorthand, branches, tags, and commit references.

faq.question: Should I use a branch or a tag?
faq.answer: Use a tag or commit for production. Branches can move and change the installed code.

faq.question: Does this work with private repositories?
faq.answer: Yes. Private repositories require SSH keys, token authentication, or npm configuration with proper permissions.

faq.question: Are Git-based npm installs safe?
faq.answer: They can be safe when the repository is trusted, pinned, reviewed, and locked.

faq.question: Will npm run package scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. Git installs can run lifecycle scripts, including prepare, from the downloaded package.

faq.question: What should I avoid?
faq.answer: Avoid hardcoded tokens, mutable production branches, unnecessary sudo, and installing unreviewed repositories.
